summary: Today’s pulse tracks George Osborne ‘thought Peter Thiel’s Bayeux tapestry visit would be secret’, MS Now, CNN and Politico say their reporters have been denied access to White House, and CNN, MS NOW, Politico reporters denied access to White House following Trump ban. Across Guardian, NPR, and BBC, the strongest repeated signals are museum, would, and house. In the background, Thick smoke seen near Riyadh airport after air-raid alerts in Saudi capital and Jewish heirs of Holocaust victims sue California museum over Nazi-looted art keep the wider picture in motion.

headlines.title: George Osborne ‘thought Peter Thiel’s Bayeux tapestry visit would be secret’
headlines.description: British Museum chair tells Big Brue festival he thought no one would find out about the private viewing George Osborne has said he thought no one would find out about a private viewing of the Bayeux tapestry he organised for the tech billionaire Peter Thiel at the British Museum. The former chancellor, who is chair of the museum, told the Big Brue festival in Somerset that he had been on holiday when the Thiel was shown the medieval artwork.

headlines.title: MS Now, CNN and Politico say their reporters have been denied access to White House
headlines.description: President said he was banning journalists from those organizations, saying of their coverage: ‘You get sick of it.’ Journalists from three US outlets were denied access to the White House grounds on Saturday morning a day after Donald Trump said he would ban them from the executive branch complex in a move that has prompted outrage and shock from free speech advocates. The outlets were television broadcasters MS now and CNN as well as the political news website Politico.

headlines.title: CNN, MS NOW, Politico reporters denied access to White House following Trump ban
headlines.description: Three reporters were blocked from the White House grounds Saturday morning, a day after President Trump said CNN, Politico, and MS NOW would be banned for reporting "FICTION and LIES."

headlines.title: Thick smoke seen near Riyadh airport after air-raid alerts in Saudi capital
headlines.description: Authorities also issued warnings for Jeddah and Yanbu, a major industrial port and home to vital oil facilities Flames and a large plume of black smoke were seen rising above Riyadh airport in Saudi Arabia on Saturday after the government sent air-raid alerts to citizens by phone overnight warning of aerial attacks. Explosions were heard in the capital and firefighters battled to extinguish the flames of a burning fuel tank emblazoned with the logo of the Saudi oil company Aramco near the city’s King Khalid international airport.

headlines.title: Jewish heirs of Holocaust victims sue California museum over Nazi-looted art
headlines.description: Pasadena’s Norton Simon Museum holds 16th-century paintings stolen by the Nazis during the second world war Jewish heirs of Holocaust victims and their representatives have filed two lawsuits in California staking their claims to Nazi -looted paintings that still hang on the walls of prominent museums in Los Angeles and Auschwitz. This pair of lawsuits are the first to be filed after the recent passage of laws by California and the US Congress, which strengthen US-based claims to artwork that were forcibly taken from Jewish families during the second world war.

headlines.title: Google's Gemini AI hacked three companies in security test
headlines.description: The AI model accessed the internet and guessed credentials to three websites, a Google official told the BBC.

headlinePool.title: Trump’s battle to rename the Kennedy Center has put its future at risk
headlinePool.description: The president has threatened to block renovations and suggested the landmark could be demolished after courts ruled against his bid to rename it It was born with the world premiere of Leonard Bernstein’s Mass. “Young people will come here and they will see this cultural centre,” Rose Kennedy, the mother of slain US president John F Kennedy, said at that opening night gala . “They will carry some of these ideas back to their different communities.” More than half a century later, the potential death knell came just after 4.30pm on Tuesday with a perfunctory announcement on the public address system: “The centre is now closed to the public. Please exit the centre by way of the Hall of States.” Soon barricades had been erected and security guards were blocking access.

headlinePool.title: Likelihood of eating fresh produce increases with income for US adults, new CDC report shows
headlinePool.description: The report highlights deep divides between low- and middle- income, a disparity that dates back decades A new report from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) reaffirms that adults are more likely to eat fresh fruits and vegetables as their income increases. The data brief comes as Republican cuts to food assistance programs, colloquially called “food stamps”, have led enrollment to “ plummet ”. Changes to US dietary guidelines, led by health secretary Robert F Kennedy Jr , have also made a government-recommended diet more expensive. A new “food pyramid” released in January emphasized animal protein, fresh fruit and vegetables, all of which cost more, according to studies.

headlinePool.title: Scottish Labour’s new leader backs Rosebank and Jackdaw oil and gasfields
headlinePool.description: Michael Marra supports development of the North Sea sites, calling for a ‘more rational’ approach to energy policy Scottish Labour’s new leader Michael Marra has backed the development of the Rosebank and Jackdaw oil and gasfields in the North Sea in one of his first acts after being elected, calling for a “more rational” approach to energy policy. On Saturday, the MSP for North East Scotland won a near two-thirds majority to lead the party in Holyrood, becoming Scottish Labour’s 11th leader. He replaces Anas Sarwar after his shock decision to resign in July to join Andy Burnham’s new government as a trade minister.

headlinePool.title: ‘Way too many guns around’: experts say firearm access key factor in spate of US family killings
headlinePool.description: Acts of ‘familicide’ have increased dramatically this year – in the US, the killer is more likely to have easy access to a gun The US is often known globally for its shocking levels of violence, but acts of “family annihilation” or “familicide” rank among the most disturbing of crimes. They occur when an assailant kills four or more of their own family members and often see the killer also kill themselves. These types of crime have increased dramatically this year, according to data from Northeastern University .

headlinePool.title: Opinion: Remembering Annie Dillard, nature writer
headlinePool.description: With her 1974 book, "Pilgrim at Tinker Creek," Annie Dillard became the youngest woman to win the Pulitzer Prize. We take a moment to remember her and her work.

headlinePool.title: US fashion CEO resigns after physically restraining animal rights activists
headlinePool.description: Steven Kolb of the Council of Fashion Designers of America was filmed during an altercation at New York fashion week The chief executive of the Council of Fashion Designers of America, Steven Kolb, has resigned after he was filmed physically restraining two animal rights activists during an altercation at New York fashion week. “After 20 years leading the CFDA, I have made the difficult decision to step down as CEO and president,” Kolb said in a statement. “I am enormously proud of what we have built together and believe this is the right moment for both me and the organisation to begin a new chapter.”

headlinePool.title: 'Enough is enough': Women protest after string of murders near Johannesburg
headlinePool.description: The police have since set up a task team to investigate the murders and have urged women in the Kempton Park area to avoid walking or running alone "particularly in isolated areas".

headlinePool.title: Shark attack prompts rare kill order in Western Australia as victim named
headlinePool.description: Greg O'Neill "loved the ocean", his family say, as police boats and helicopters patrol Perth's beaches in search of his body and the shark that attacked him.

headlinePool.title: Life in Kabul 5 years after the Taliban's return
headlinePool.description: Five years after the return of Taliban rule, NPR visited Kabul to see how Afghans are dealing with their new government's strict social restrictions.
